A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TTC-Net research despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison; v2 principally extends Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original Sudoku and mathematical reasoning experiments, component ablations, and LQR solver throughput and memory measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds decoding comparisons, broader benchmarks, Qwen results, inference throughput measurements, and latent-state analyses.

M1.justification: The TTC architecture, contextualized LQR parameterization, differentiable symplectic solver, training objectives, and horizon-sampling strategy are unchanged. Applying TTC to Qwen and adding diagnostic probes do not establish changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Table 7 adds evaluation on HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Challenge, MMLU, and HumanEval. This substantially broadens evaluated task requirements beyond Sudoku and mathematical problem solving to commonsense, knowledge, and code generation. The original training data and evaluation benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix D.2 and Table 5 add evaluated Best-of-N and Tree-of-Thoughts baselines, introducing external decoding/search methods alongside the retained architectural and solver comparisons. Self-consistency and RAP are discussed and cited but are not reported as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include accuracy/token-use comparisons, a TTC-by-CoT prompting experiment, Qwen2.5-Math-7B evaluation, H100 inference throughput across planning horizons, linear probing, and trajectory alignment with random-pair controls. Original splits, training settings, and evaluation procedures are retained. The H100 inference experiment supplements the existing H200 solver benchmark rather than replacing its hardware or protocol.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 adds a 2-by-2 TTC/explicit-CoT ablation, inference-throughput sensitivity to planning horizon, Sudoku latent-state probing, and same-question versus random-pair trajectory alignment. These investigate dependence on explicit reasoning, practical overhead, and the information encoded by latent planning states.

E5.justification: The original solver benchmark's median-runtime and 20-80% percentile reporting is retained. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Original results remain unchanged, while Tables 5-11 add substantial results. New examples include no-CoT AMC accuracy of 3.92% without TTC versus 7.83% with TTC, and Qwen MATH-500 scores of 74.4 after fine-tuning versus 75.6 with TTC. Table 7 reports mixed outcomes: HumanEval scores of 32.32 versus 49.39, but WinoGrande scores of 74.74 versus 72.09, for SFT and TTC respectively. Table 6's with-CoT scores repeat Table 2 rather than representing changed results.

T1.justification: Appendix D.6 introduces a formal trajectory-similarity definition that maximizes average cosine similarity over specified monotone alignment paths. The existing LQR definitions, propositions, theorems, derivations, and proofs in Section 3 and Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same architectural planning, solver-efficiency, and reasoning-performance claims, including the headline numerical gains. The new appendix experiments provide additional support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: The new appendix substantially expands interpretation: TTC is explicitly described as complementary to, rather than a replacement for, explicit CoT; broader benchmark results are interpreted as preserving general capabilities; and probe/alignment findings are interpreted as progressive refinement and internalized reasoning. It also discusses end-to-end inference costs across horizons. Section 6's original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the exact prompt suppressing explicit CoT, identifies H100 hardware for the new inference benchmark, and describes extracting TTC trajectories from the first token after the prompt. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, and data-curation details are retained. Search budgets, probe training settings, and full inference configurations remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds references to Stiennon et al. (2020), Wang et al. (2022), Yao et al. (2024), and Hao et al. (2023), positioning TTC relative to external sampling and search. This is a localized expansion; the existing discussions of differentiable control, TTD, world models, and continuous CoT remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes to 'Beyond Test-Time Memory: State-Space Optimal Control for LLM Reasoning.' Appendix D becomes 'More Experiments,' with the original details retained as D.1 and new subsections D.2-D.6 appended. Cross-references are updated, while the existing main narrative and Appendices A-C are essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the appendix's displays with Tables 5-11 covering decoding, CoT ablation, general benchmarks, Qwen, throughput, and latent-state analyses, plus a boxed prompt. Existing Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-4 retain their content and design, with only limited surrounding reflow.

improvement.justification: The broader benchmark and backbone evaluations, CoT ablation, and end-to-end timing provide useful checks of applicability and practical cost that v1 lacked. Their evidential value is limited by unspecified search budgets, probe settings, and inference configurations, alongside unchanged uncertainty reporting. The latent correlations also provide narrower support than the interpretation of internalized reasoning suggests. The additions improve validation, but these reporting and interpretation limitations keep the overall gain modest.
